title: Consistency profiles: Luka is the league's steadiest star
headline_insight: Of 579 qualified players, Luka Doncic is the most consistent game to game, with a shrunk composite coefficient of variation of 0.3448 -- well under the league median of 0.6235 -- edging out Nikola Jokic at 0.3456.
what_it_means: Consistency is measured as the coefficient of variation (spread relative to average) of per-36 points, rebounds, and assists across a player's games, shrunk toward the league mean for players with fewer games. Doncic and Jokic sitting at the top means their nightly production barely wobbles -- roughly half the game-to-game variability of a median rotation player -- which is exactly what you'd expect from high-usage engines who touch the ball every possession. Low volatility is not the same as high value: a low-minute role player can post a steady, small stat line too.
how_to_read: composite_cv_shrunk is the headline number (lower = steadier); compare each player against the distribution's median of 0.6235.
why_it_matters: Game-to-game variance is the raw ingredient of any player-prop or projection interval -- knowing who is metronomic versus streaky shapes how wide those intervals should be.
caveat: DESCRIPTIVE_ONLY and NOT predictive: CV inflates mechanically for low-mean stats, so rebound/assist CVs are not on the same scale as points across archetypes, and no opponent/rest/role adjustment is applied.
